definitions.explanation: The price of a single item or unit.

examples.japanese: {客|きゃく}{単価|たんか}を{上|あ}げる{戦略|せんりゃく}を{考|かんが}える。
examples.english: To think of strategies to increase customer spending.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つあたりの{単価|たんか}は200{円|えん}だ。
examples.english: The unit price is 200 yen each.

notes:
{単価|たんか} refers to the price of a single unit or item. It is primarily used in business, retail, and manufacturing contexts rather than everyday conversation.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {客|きゃく}{単価|たんか}: average spending per customer (a key retail metric)
- {単価|たんか}が{高|たか}い/{安|やす}い: high/low unit price
- {単価|たんか}を{上|あ}げる/{下|さ}げる: to raise/lower the unit price
- {原価|げんか}{単価|たんか}: unit cost (manufacturing)

COMPONENTS:
{単|たん} (single) + {価|か} (price). Related terms include {定価|ていか} (list price), {原価|げんか} (cost price), and {時価|じか} (market price).

USAGE:
In business discussions, {客|きゃく}{単価|たんか} (customer unit price) is a key performance metric meaning the average amount each customer spends per visit or transaction.
